title: Where Coffee Comes From
description: Coffee grows in the Bean Belt — between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.

title: Arabica vs Robusta
description: Arabica is smooth and complex; Robusta is strong and bitter. Most specialty coffee is Arabica.

title: Green Coffee
description: Unroasted beans stay fresh for months during shipping. Roasting happens close to the consumer.

title: Washed Processing
description: Fruit removed before drying produces clean, bright cups that highlight origin character.

title: Natural Processing
description: Whole cherries dried in the sun develop fruity, wine-like flavors from the fermenting fruit.

title: Honey Processing
description: Some fruit mucilage stays on the bean during drying — a balance of washed clarity and natural sweetness.

title: What Roasting Does
description: Heat triggers hundreds of chemical reactions that create coffee's aroma, flavor, and color.

title: Light Roast
description: Roasted to first crack — high acidity, floral and fruity notes, most origin character preserved.

title: Medium Roast
description: Balanced between origin and roast flavors: caramel, nuts, and milk chocolate with moderate acidity.

title: Dark Roast
description: Past second crack: oily beans, low acidity, heavy body, dark chocolate and smoke notes.

title: Grind Size
description: Fine for espresso, medium for pour-over, coarse for French press. Grind size controls extraction speed.

title: Water Temperature
description: 90–96°C is the ideal brewing range for filter coffee. Too hot scorches; too cool under-extracts.

title: Brew Ratio
description: Grams of coffee to grams of water. A 1:15 ratio (e.g., 20g coffee to 300g water) is a common starting point.

title: Extraction
description: 18–22% extraction yield is the sweet spot. Sour = under. Bitter = over. Adjust grind, time, or temperature.

title: Acidity, Body & Sweetness
description: The three core sensory axes of coffee: brightness, texture, and the natural sugar balance.

title: How to Taste Coffee
description: Slurp to aerate, note what you perceive, and taste again as it cools — flavors shift with temperature.

title: Flavor Descriptors
description: The SCA flavor wheel gives tasters a shared language: floral, fruity, nutty, caramel, chocolate, smoky.
